newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Jardine expects more profits, seen leaner.
newsitem.headline: Jardine expects more profits, seen leaner.

text.p: Jardine Davies Inc is expected to rake in more profits in 1997 due to better prospects with a leaner portfolio, officials said on Wednesday.
"The benefits of the increased focus on the core businesses of the group should be seen in a rebound in profitability in 1997," chairman Aloysius Colayco told shareholders at their annual meeting.
The net income of the company in the first quarter of the year rose sharply to 237.978 million pesos against 8.035 million in the same period last year.
The company's net in the first three months of the year was boosted by non-recurring income of 227.51 million pesos, vice president Rufino Melo reported to shareholders.

The non-recurring income involves the sale Jardine Davies' 40 percent stake in Jardine CMG Life Insurance Co to its joint venture partner Colonial Limited of Australia, senior vice president for finance David Clymo said.
The exit of Jardine Davies from the insurance business was part of the group's restructuring, Clymo said.

The firm's interests in Jardine Aboitiz Insurance Brokers, Jardine Wines and Spirits, Thorn Ligthing and Jardine Davies Transport Services were also transferred to other companies of the Jardine group, the company said in a report to stockholders.
Colayco said Jardine Davies will focus on building and industrial materials, development of middle-income housing, agribusiness, consumer finance and stock broking as its core businesses this year.
